tests.notes: only the selected branch runs, so only its side effects happen; a converter lowering ?: to a branch-free select would run both calls
the division in the unselected branch never evaluates, so b == 0 ? 0 : a / b does not panic with 0x12
i < items.length ? items[i] : 0 never evaluates the out-of-bounds read (Panic 0x32) when the check fails
the result type is the wider of the two branch types; the narrower branch is implicitly widened
literal branches take the smallest unsigned type that holds each literal and the result is the wider of the two (255/256 gives uint16)
?: is right-associative: a ? x : b ? y : z is a ? x : (b ? y : z)
the condition can be any bool expression; comparisons and logical operators bind tighter than ?:
a conditional expression can be a function argument or an operand of another operator when parenthesized
branches may read or modify storage; used as a statement, useHigh ? high++ : low++ increments exactly one counter
memory array branches of the same type are allowed; the result is a reference to the chosen array, so writing through it modifies the original
string literal branches of different lengths give a common string memory result; string memory variables work as branches too
compiles successfully; abs(type(int256).min) reverts with Panic(0x11) because the negation overflows
casting a branch gives both branches the same type; the fix for the rejected shapes in 021 and 024
a conditional expression is allowed in a constant's initializer when everything in it is constant
compiles successfully; f(true, 255, 1) does not revert because a + b in the unselected branch is not evaluated, f(false, 255, 1) reverts with Panic(0x11)
the condition must be bool; integers have no truthiness
uint256 and int256 branches have no common type; fix by casting one branch (see 017)
a bool branch and an integer branch have no common type
1 and 256 give result type uint16, so assigning to uint8 narrows even if the 256 branch is never taken (contrast with 006)
the literal -1 is int8 and 1 is uint8, which have no common type even with an int256 target; fix by casting a branch (see 017)
a conditional expression is a value, not a location, so it cannot be assigned to
both branches are mandatory; there is no one-armed conditional expression

a uint8 branch with an int16 branch is rejected by solc 0.8.36 even though uint8 assigns to int16 implicitly elsewhere; ?: does not apply signed/unsigned widening to its branches, only same-signedness widening (see 005)
